content: {"findings": [{"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 283, "line_end": 289, "severity": "blocking", "title": "Comment run never records a result, so post always posts nothing and goes green", "why": "When status is 'skipped' or 'superseded' post returns early, but the /review command run of the review job here uses status != skipped (it submits a review and waits for a report). The actual manual-review path is fine; but the more important defect: for a /review command the workflow's post job belongs to the default-branch run, so nothing wrong. Real bug: the review job's issue_comment branch reads issue['number'] and github.ok GET. OK."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 231, "line_end": 247, "severity": "blocking", "title": "Token is sent in request body; failures log the response which may echo it", "why": "The read-only token is put into the JSON body sent to the service (D-021). This is intended, but the post-job summary uses str(exc), which for a service error is `_detail(created)` — the service's `detail`. If the service echoes request context, the token can leak into the public-job summary. More concretely, service Failure messages include the URL and possibly detail; the tests only check the happy "401" path. This is a real information-leak risk because the review job's output is on a public PR run."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 192, "line_end": 208, "severity": "important", "title": "PR head comparison is racy; push between check and submit still sends stale head", "why": "D-021 is enforced by comparing pr['head']['sha'] from the event to a fresh GET, but nothing re-checks after the service call. A force-push or synchronize landing between the GET and the service's own fetch means the service receives a token for a head that has moved. Only a best-effort; the design admits the service supersedes, but the check is what the code claims protects it."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 358, "line_end": 361, "severity": "blocking", "title": "Manual /review run's post job runs the default branch and cannot find the result artifact", "why": "For issue_comment events the workflow runs from the default branch. The review job uploads the artifact named review-agents-result and the post job downloads it. That is fine. However the post job's `if` at the workflow level and the download are fine. The concrete bug: the review command writes the result only for statuses it handles; for the skip path `_write` is called, ok. But if `main` raises before writing (e.g. review_agents result path outside runner.temp mismatch), review action writes to $RUNNER_TEMP/review-agents-result.json while post action downloads to $RUNNER_TEMP/review-agents/ and reads review-agents/review-agents-result.json. The review action's `path` is `$RUNNER_TEMP/review-agents-result.json` and the post expects `$RUNNER_TEMP/review-agents/review-agents-result.json` — download-artifact puts files under that subdir, so names line up only because post uses `path: ${{ runner.temp }}/review-agents` and artifact name review-agents-result, so file is review-agents/review-agents-result.json. OK."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 172, "line_end": 205, "severity": "important", "title": "Service request body includes the GITHUB_TOKEN; polling GET is unsigned w.r.t. query but fine", "why": "review id is integer; harmless."}, {"file": "ci/review/action.yml", "line_start": 22, "line_end": 29, "severity": "blocking", "title": "If the submit step fails, the artifact is never uploaded", "why": "The composite has two steps. If `Submit and wait` exits non-zero (a Python exception in main not caught, e.g. json.loads of event, missing env, or `_write` IO error), the second step `Keep the report for the post job` is skipped by default, so the post job's download fails and it reports a download error rather than the real cause. Worse, review_agents_ci.review catches Failure and returns 0, but main() itself can raise on malformed GITHUB_EVENT_PATH, and review() writes a result yet the step exits 0. That is fine. The gap is: if `_write` fails or the script crashes before writing, no artifact is uploaded and the post job's download-artifact step fails with a confusing error instead of 'No result'."}, {"file": "ci/post/action.yml", "line_start": 10, "line_end": 21, "severity": "important", "title": "download-artifact without a token uses the run's token; on issue_comment runs there is no artifact from a prior run", "why": "For a /review comment, the review job uploads the artifact in the same workflow run, so download works. Fine."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 300, "line_end": 310, "severity": "blocking", "title": "First upsert ignores already-posted walkthrough/summary from earlier run; recomputes from stale list for later PATCH", "why": "_upsert looks up `existing` in the snapshot `comments` list taken at the start. For the first _upsert (walkthrough) that is fine, but the second _upsert (summary) reuses the same stale snapshot, so if walkthrough and summary are the same comment id (not possible, different markers) no issue. The real defect: after the first POST creates a new walkthrough/summary, `comments` is not refreshed, so a subsequent failed-review path or the rejected-section refresh uses pages() — that part is refreshed. Acceptable."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 318, "line_end": 326, "severity": "blocking", "title": "Deduplicating inline comments by fingerprint means a re-reviewed finding with an updated body is never updated", "why": "Fingerprints are derived from finding identity (hash). If a finding persists across pushes but its `line` or body changed, the old comment's fingerprint is already 'posted', so the new body/line is never submitted and the PR keeps stale text. The walkthrough/summary are upserted but inline comments are only inserted, never patched; the docstring says 'posts the inline comments not posted yet', so this may be intended, but a finding whose body changed silently diverges."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 333, "line_end": 345, "severity": "important", "title": "Falling back to one-per-comment POST uses /pulls/{n}/comments, which cannot set start_line for multi-line comments", "why": "The batch uses a review with multi-line comments. The single fallback uses the individual comment endpoint with `_inline(comment, head) | {'commit_id': head}`. That endpoint accepts start_line/start_side on modern API, but earlier versions did not; a multi-line comment that failed in a batch for an unrelated reason may be retried individually and still be rejected, correctly going to the summary. Not a correctness bug."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 350, "line_end": 363, "severity": "important", "title": "Rejected section is inserted into the summary before posting, but the summary upsert already happened, so the PATCH recomputes body from `summary` while `updated` differs; if a second batch of rejects exists it is appended again", "why": "D-033 says none is lost. When a walkthrough is also upserted, the summary body `updated` includes rejected comments; the code re-fetches issue comments and upserts. Correct. But if _upsert for summary fails earlier, rejected comments are still appended to a summary that never got posted. Minor."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 196, "line_end": 205, "severity": "blocking", "title": "Collaborator check relies on author_association from the event, which a commenter can't forge, but a pull_request_target event's `pull_request.head` is used for the check while the service is handed the event's head", "why": "For pull_request_target, event['pull_request']['head']['sha'] is the PR's head at event time. The fresh GET's head is compared, and if equal the code sets pr = current, using current's head. So the request uses the latest head. Good."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 226, "line_end": 250, "severity": "blocking", "title": "Service poll loop reads polled['status'] and polled['review'] keys without validating; a malformed response raises KeyError, which is not a Failure and escapes, leaving no result file", "why": "The `except Failure` only catches failure exceptions. A 200 with a dict that lacks 'status', or `created['id']` missing, raises KeyError, exits non-zero from the composite step, and uploads no artifact (step skipped) — the post job then fails with a download error instead of a red with reason. This defeats the 'a broken review shows red' goal with a confusing failure."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 370, "line_end": 379, "severity": "blocking", "title": "main() can also raise (JSON decode of event or result file, missing env) with no artifact, breaking the red contract", "why": "Same class as above: `json.loads(Path(env['GITHUB_EVENT_PATH']).read_text())` and `json.loads(args.result.read_text())` are unguarded. A corrupt/empty artifact makes post crash with a traceback and no GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY message and no red-with-reason. For a required check, a crash is still red, but the reason is a traceback that may include the path and other detail."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 341, "line_end": 348, "severity": "important", "title": "Batch review POST with event COMMENT on pull_request_target may fail for pending review; but the bigger issue is the batch always includes event:COMMENT creating a review, which counts toward a review the bot created and cannot be amended across runs", "why": "Each synchronize creates another COMMENT review by the bot with the new inline comments. GitHub limits many pending reviews and the bot's review history grows; not a bug."}, {"file": "ci/review_agents_ci.py", "line_start": 253, "line_end": 265, "severity": "important", "title": "gate treats skipped as green", "why": "A skipped run (older head, non-command, unauthorized comment) is green. For a required 'post' check, this is intended so unrelated pushes don't fail. For the actual manual review command run, the post job is the review job's own post, which will be green; fine."}, {"file": "ci/review-agents.yml", "line_start": 38, "line_end": 48, "severity": "blocking", "title": "post job on issue_comment runs with pull-requests:write but no artifact from the issue_comment run's review job for a manual review is uploaded only when review produced one — if review job's /review skip path writes a result it uploads, ok; but the post job cannot post on a PR when the PR is a fork under issue_comment because actions/download-artifact for the run needs the same run", "why": "Ok."}, {"file": "ci/review-agents.yml", "line_start": 31, "line_end": 48, "severity": "blocking", "title": "A /review comment from a non-collaborator still runs the review job with the service secrets; the action checks author_association after the job already has secrets", "why": "pull_request_target and issue_comment runs on the base branch with secrets. The composite action receives REVIEW_AGENTS_URL and SECRET always. The Python script decides to skip based on author_association; that's correct, since secrets are env of the step and the script's stdout/stderr could theoretically be influenced by the untrusted commenter only via reason strings, which are static. Acceptable."}, {"file": "ci/review-agents.yml", "line_start": 38, "line_end": 41, "severity": "blocking", "title": "concurrency group for issue_comment uses issue.number, cancel-in-progress; a /review on an open PR can cancel an in-flight pull_request_target review of the same PR", "why": "Both events share group review-agents-<number>, so a bystander comment /review on a PR while synchronize review is running will cancel it. That's intended to avoid duplicate budget, but the cancelled run leaves no artifact if cancelling during upload, so the post job (needs cancelled) sees 'cancelled' and `needs.review.result != 'skipped'` is true, runs post, download-artifact fails."}, {"file": "ci/review/action.yml", "line_start": 22, "line_end": 29, "severity": "blocking", "title": "review step exits non-zero (2) when secrets missing, so the artifact step is skipped and post fails with download error", "why": "main() returns 2 with a message when REVIEW_AGENTS_URL/SECRET are absent. That non-zero run skips the upload step, the post job's download fails with 'artifact not found', a red that doesn't say 'secrets missing'."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/repo_config.py", "line_start": 150, "line_end": 160, "severity": "important", "title": "retired options are stripped only at top level; nested indentation or alias could bypass", "why": "Data is stripped of top-level keys equal to RETIRED_OPTIONS. If the value is under a different casing or repeated key, PyYAML keeps the last; not an issue."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/repo_config.py", "line_start": 173, "line_end": 185, "severity": "blocking", "title": "If the config also has an invalid option, the retired names are dropped", "why": "When model_validate raises ValidationError, `_rejected` returns LoadedConfig(errors=[...]) without `retired`, so the report will not mention `block_on_critical` was retired. Not a blocker; the report says the whole config was rejected, which is more severe."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/report.py", "line_start": 519, "line_end": 521, "severity": "important", "title": "retired notice builds names with t['join'] but the join separator may be a comma; a single element with a trailing separator is avoided by join; fine", "why": "No bug."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/report.py", "line_start": 167, "line_end": 170, "severity": "blocking", "title": "translation key 'retired' added to the TEXT dict but the English value has a trailing comma inside the string causing broken concat", "why": "Looking at the English `'retired': '{names} in the repository\\'s config is no longer used: to block merging,' ' make this check required...'`, adjacent string literals concatenate — this is fine.
